claims.claim: Deterministic workflow and carrier tests prove that one successful GitHub-Issue SUBMIT_REVIEW canonicalization produces exactly one bounded wakeup request to the existing safe Publisher using only the canonical RUN selector, with no direct main mutation or candidate selection in the ingress carrier.
AUTHOR_TASK, AUTHOR_REMEDIATION, AUTHOR_REPAIR, rejected ingress, malformed carrier events, and ingress exceptions produce no publication wakeup.

Publication continuation does not rely on the review-decision push trigger and works from the same GITHUB_TOKEN-based Issue workflow context with actions: write permission without PAT or external secret authority, while transport acceptance remains distinguishable from publication result.

The existing Publisher independently re-resolves canonical review-decision and source RUN and retains all safe-publication protections; no review verdict, candidate SHA, target ref, force flag, or publication command is accepted from Issue content or carrier output.
Identical SUBMIT_REVIEW replay cannot publish twice or choose a new candidate, and a CHANGES_REQUIRED non-publishable decision cannot advance main.

Existing Issue ingress, file/stdin ingress, publication workflow_dispatch fallback, publication.py regressions, TASK-108 PRIMARY wakeup, and A6 REMEDIATION behavior remain compatible with no new generic lifecycle router or semantic authority introduced.
Required focused verification and git diff --check pass with no modified file outside TASK-110 scope and RESULT contains zero unresolved items.
